text:
Ravi: @Ashley looping you in — TerraceAI is asking for a Dedicated reservation but with large, short-lived campaign spikes. They gave a baseline and a peak profile; need sizing guidance + a safe burst policy so sales can finish the PO today.
Ashley: quick q — which region(s) and model quantization? latency SLO?
Ravi: primary us-west-2, backup eu-west-1. Model: 7B quantized (int8-ish), avg prompt+resp ~120 tokens. They want p99-ish latency <250ms for chat. Baseline 120 GPU-hrs/day, during campaign days they expect ~600 GPU-hrs concentrated into ~6h windows.
Luis: rough capacity calc below. short answer: baseline ~5 GPUs steady, campaign peak ~100 GPUs for the 6h window. If we only reserve ~8-12 GPUs you need a large burst pool or hot pool for campaign days.
Luis: ```
baseline = 120 GPU-hrs/day -> 120/24 = 5 GPUs
peak_total = 600 GPU-hrs over 6h -> 600/6 = 100 GPUs simultaneous
recommendation (quick): reserved_commit = 12 GPUs (2.4x baseline)
burst_needed = ~88 GPUs during campaign windows
warm/sync buffer ~= 10-15% (~9-13 GPUs)
```
Marta: ops note: cross-region failover + model sync means pre-warm time and network egress. For eu-west failover we'd need model replicas ready or cold-starts will kill p99. Add ~10-15% headroom for warm replicas and sync bandwidth. Also we should enforce per-customer burst caps (token-bucket) so a single campaign can't rocket other customers.
Anna: from solutions perspective customers prefer a simple offer: (A) commit X GPUs monthly + (B) pre-scheduled burst days with guaranteed hot pool at a premium + (C) on-demand burst at a higher rate. That maps cleanly to our Dedicated pricing tiers.
Ashley: operationally I don't want to promise 100 GPUs without a plan for locking capacity. Options: 1) Reserve 12 GPUs + provide a scheduled hot pool for campaign days (we spin up extra 80 GPUs with 24h notice, priced higher), 2) Reserve 40 GPUs (higher monthly commit) so live bursts are limited, 3) Hybrid: reserved 12 + smaller hot pool + allow on-demand beyond that with burst throttles. Each has cost/SL tradeoffs.
Ravi: can you convert option 1 into estimated cost delta so I can pass to finance? Also we need the burst SLA and whether we can guarantee p99 <250ms.
Luis: ballpark numbers: reserved GPU hour list-price (hosted) ~$X/hr -> reserved discount makes it ~$0.7X/hr. Example: reserve 12 GPUs -> 12*24*30 * 0.7X = ~6048 * 0.7X GPU-hrs price-equivalent. Hot pool: 80 GPUs for 6h on campaign day -> 80*6 = 480 GPU-hrs per campaign day at on-demand (~X/hr). If they run 4 campaign days / month -> 480*4 = 1920 GPU-hrs on-demand. network egress + pre-warm labor add ~5-10% on top.
Marta: we should also include a safety clause: if cluster util >85% we may delay non-critical spin-ups; we need an escalation path for TerraceAI if campaign scaling is blocked.
deploy-bot: capacity-alert: reserved-pool-us-west-2 at 85% utilization right now.
Ashley: noted. I'll draft an offer: commit 12 GPUs monthly + scheduled hot pool (80 GPUs) available with 24h notice, on-demand beyond that at standard burst rate, 12 GPU warm buffer included. Include failover plan to eu-west-1 with cold-start window up to 30m unless they pay for pre-warmed replicas.
Ravi: perfect — can you drop that into a short attachment and I’ll send to TerraceAI legal today? Also cc @Anna for the implementation checklist. :+1:
Anna: will prepare the checklist (model transfer steps, pre-warm runbook, billing flags).
Ashley: scheduling a quick sync at 15:00 PT to finalize numbers.
Ravi: ack, thanks everyone.
